items.body:
The supermarket chain Iceland has said it will open a shop on the Falkland Islands in early December.
The shop, to be launched in partnership with a local retailer, Kelper Stores, will be the first UK high street brand to have a presence in the British territory and will be in the capital, Stanley.
Richard Walker, the retailer’s executive chair, said the company was “proud to be backing Britain”.
“The Falklands are a special part of the British family and it’s always been an ambition of mine to support it, so being able to bring Iceland to Stanley is a huge moment for us,” Lord Walker said. “This is an important moment for the business and our international aspirations.
“I will personally be visiting the Falklands to officially open the store and I’m looking forward to welcoming our new customers through the door.”
Iceland’s plan comes less than a week after the Argentine president, Javier Milei, stepped up his nation’s sovereignty claims over the islands.
“Recently, President Trump declared that the US is re-evaluating its historic position in relation to the Malvinas,” Milei said, using the Argentinian name for the Falklands.
He said the UK was facing “multiple crises of a migratory, demographic and economic nature that are unlikely to be resolved. It is clear that they are on a path of decline. Argentina’s future, however, is flourishing and will prevail.”
Milei pledged to impose sanctions on oil companies drilling in the territory, with his government confirming on Monday that it would file criminal charges against the Israeli energy company Navitas Petroleum and its executives for operating in the Falklands.
Meanwhile, a local fishing company, Fortuna, and the Danish company F-land ApS have faced local opposition to a joint venture to build a salmon farm in the region, primarily around environmental concerns. Salmon Free Falklands, set up by local people to oppose the proposal, is calling for a referendum on the project.

items.title: John Lewis chair bemoans higher cost of doing business as losses more than double
items.summary: The department store and Waitrose owner said that losses for the first half of the year to 1 August were £89 million - compared to £34m last year. It blamed rising costs such as National Insurance.
items.body:
John Lewis chair bemoans higher cost of doing business as losses more than double
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
John Lewis is nursing losses that more than doubled in the first half of the year as its boss criticised the higher cost of doing business.
The retailer reported losses of £89million in the six months to 1 August - compared to £34million a year earlier.
Chairman Jason Tarry pointed to the 'increased costs of doing business', which includes the rising cost of employment following the increase in National Insurance contributions for employers.
Profits were also hit by the costs of managing the business during the succession of heatwaves over the summer.
But Tarry insisted a turnaround was still underway and that the employee-owned partnership had been keen to keep investing in its shops despite pressures.
John Lewis: The department shop has been investing in a refresh to appeal to beauty and health demands
Sales across the group rose 2 per cent to £6.3 billion as strong trading at Waitrose offset a decline at John Lewis.
Meanwhile, sales at the department store sales dropped 2 per cent as consumers were reluctant to fork out on big-ticket items such as furniture.
The 'subdued' market prompted more promotions and clearance discounts too.
Investments into John Lewis shops also hit profits, including new looks for shops in Cambridge and Leicester. Its refresh includes adding trendier sportswear brands to appeal to health conscious Gen Z shoppers and massive beauty halls, including in Liverpool and Oxford Street.
Tarry said: ‘Our first-half results reflect our continued investment in our transformation, a more challenging trading environment and the increased costs of doing business.’
He joined a chorus of business leaders speaking out amid fears that Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Chancellor John Healey are plotting a fresh business rates raid on large shops – including stores such as John Lewis – to fund lower bills for pubs and music venues.
Shops should not pay more, retailers say, and they are particularly concerned that rates paid by large stores, which are deemed to have a rateable value of £500,000 or more, will be increased.
On Thursday, Tarry called on the Government to deliver on its promises to revive the High Street and reform business rates.
He said that in many cases both John Lewis and Waitrose shops are a ‘destination’ on High Streets, drawing footfall into shops.
‘The rebalancing that is being talked about around small store relief for large stores would mean that those anchor stores would be caught in business rate increases. Reform is the thing that we would ask for.’
The commercial property levy was the biggest tax faced by the partnership and in some locations its shops pay more in rates than in rent, making it an ‘issue’ for the business, he added.
Former managing director Peter Ruis, who left last week, said it would be 'terrible' for the industry.
Speaking last week, Ruis said: ‘It would have a terrible impact for all retailers. A lot of the smaller stores that won’t be affected by that are against it because they need people like us.
The business historically makes the majority of its profits in the second half, during its peak Christmas trading period, and said it was 'set up well'.
Tarry said that the John Lewis business was in the ‘earlier stages’ of its transformation but there was evidence to show investment in glossier shops is paying off compared to the rest of the estate.
But this morning's update could spark concerns as to whether it will offer staff a bonus next year. John Lewis brought back the employee for the first time in four years last year, in a coup for bosses leading the turnaround.
The business was seen to have lost its way under former bosses, focusing on non-retail ventures such as a build-to-rent property division while rival Marks and Spencer poached shoppers.
Together, Tarry and Ruis, have seen signs of a revival, including by investing in shops and bringing back its historic ‘Never Knowingly Undersold’ pledge.
Consumer confidence has been hit by higher fuel prices triggered by the war in Iran while hopes for interest rate reductions at the start of the year have since faded, Tarry said.
But he said it was a positive sign that the Budget this year is in late October - compared to last year’s which was in late November and coincided with Black Friday.
Ahead of the 28 October Budget, Tarry said that this year ‘we’re not seeing that level of speculation, which is causing customer concern on top of what they're already worried about.’

items.title: Primark bows to customer pressure with promise to offer home delivery in Britain
items.summary: Primark will launch home delivery for its customers as it comes under pressure from cheaper online rivals.
items.body:
Primark bows to customer pressure with promise to offer home delivery in Britain
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Primark will launch online home delivery for its customers in Britain in a bid to boost sales as it comes under pressure from cheaper online rivals.
Its owner, Associated British Foods, said the discount clothing brand, which has resisted the move for years, would offer delivery ‘in the future’.
Customers have long called for Primark, which has nearly 200 stores in the UK, to offer delivery like other high street brands with cheaper Chinese rivals, such as Shein, plugging the gap.
Primark has previously argued as recently as May that its low prices and tight margins cannot absorb the additional costs related to online delivery.
The group has moved closer to online retail in recent years, launching a mobile app for British customers earlier this year to support its overdue move into click-and-collect, which debuted in November 2022.
It had previously conceded that customers are 'increasingly turning to digital tools that make shopping easier'.
Primark promises to offer home delivery 'in the future' as online rivals ramp up pressure
In a statement this morning, owner ABF said: ‘Building on this strategy, Primark will continue to grow Click & Collect and, having undertaken a detailed review, will in the future offer home delivery in Great Britain.
‘Primark's digital maturity, including the success of Click & Collect, and online market developments, mean there is now the opportunity for profitable growth through the home delivery channel.’
ABF chief executive George Weston told City analysts on Thursday morning that he would not divulge any details about the date of starting home delivery: ‘That's pretty sensitive commercial information.’
It has bought a Sheffield fulfilment facility from Boohoo for £90million as it ramps up its online operations.
Weston said it was ‘quite a big piece of home delivery story’ and means the business can launch this service quicker than if it had to build a new hub itself.
He added: ‘The market really has come to notice in terms of pricing for delivery to people's homes. The depot will give us a good package dispatch cost base, and then the trick is to make sure that the bulk of the home delivery sales are incremental, not substitutional. We think that we've got the tools to help us along to achieving that.’
It marks a significant move by chief executive Eoin Tonge, who joined a year ago, as he prepares for Primark to be spun off from owner ABF.
An expansion of Primark's online offering came as the retailer reported a slowdown in sales and expects a 3 per cent fall in its fourth quarter to September 12.
The wider group warned that losses at its sugar business would be towards the higher end of its previous guidance range of between £25million and £60million for the current financial year.
Shares plummeted nearly 10 per cent to 1,818.5p.
Mark Crouch, market analyst at eToro said: 'Home delivery in the UK is the right call and closes a long running gap. It will not rescue this Christmas, and the market has treated it accordingly.'
Aarin Chekrie, equity analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown added that while it would help to boost Primark's top line, but 'running an efficient and profitable delivery and returns service is no easy task, doing it profitably is even more difficult.'

items.summary: Co-op Wholesale has announced a major investment in its vape proposition that will deliver lower upfront prices, a simpler commercial model for retail partners and a significantly expanded range.​ ​With the forthcoming introduction of Vaping Products Duty set to bring additional complexity to the category,… This story continues at Co-op Wholesale invests in vape category with ‘simplified value’ for retailers Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
With the forthcoming introduction of Vaping Products Duty set to bring additional complexity to the category, Co-op Wholesale is simplifying how value is delivered to retailers. 
From October 2026, the wholesaler will be reducing invoice prices by up to 15% across its vape range as well as simplifying its vape rebate model.
Designed to help retailers navigate a changing vape market, the new proposition will deliver value directly through lower purchase prices, giving retailers greater transparency and making margins easier to manage.
In addition, it will be adding over 200 new vape lines, taking its range to approximately 500 SKUs.
Katie Secretan, managing director at Co-op Wholesale, said: “Retailers are navigating significant change within the vape category. This is an opportunity for us to simplify the way we manage the commercial value of vape; from rebate to price, offering our retailers a real opportunity to grow their business.
“We are refreshing our range, to one of the biggest in the wholesale market of over 500 SKUs and investing to deliver some of the best pricing in the market too. We’re going big, to support our retailers at a time that really matters.” 
Retail partners have today (9 September) received full details of the new proposition and range, with dedicated support, account management guidance and an invite to a retailer webinar hosted by industry experts to learn more about how to navigate the upcoming vape duty.

items.title: Selling to Corporate Giants – Tessa Clarke on taking 3.5 years to land Tesco
items.summary: Tessa Clarke spent three and a half years trying to sign Tesco. Another large retailer took her six years and a third is still at the pilot stage after eight. In a fireside chat at SCALE Summit in London, Tessa talked to HelloFresh co-founder Hamish Shephard about the reality of selling into large corporates.  It’s [...]
items.body:
Selling to Corporate Giants – Tessa Clarke on taking 3.5 years to land Tesco
Tessa Clarke spent three and a half years trying to sign Tesco. Another large retailer took her six years and a third is still at the pilot stage after eight.
In a fireside chat at SCALE Summit in London, Tessa talked to HelloFresh co-founder Hamish Shephard about the reality of selling into large corporates.
It’s slow, it rarely follows the founders’ plan, and if you bet everything on closing one big commercial relationship, you are probably taking an unnecessary risk.
I’ve been reflecting on their conversation, which took place at the Business Design Centre in April, and looking forward to the Selling Into Enterprise panel happening at SCALE Manchester on 25 November. For Commercial Directors like me, these are the scaleup lessons that matter most.
Gather your evidence first
Tessa Clarke’s Olio app has rescued over 100 million meals that were destined for the bin. Led by a female-majority team, Olio tackles household and community waste by connecting neighbours so they can give away spare food and household items rather than throw them away. Olio’s growth has been driven by its business proposition: unsold food is collected from supermarkets, schools, hospitals, restaurants, and corporate canteens, then listed on the app for locals to collect within minutes.
“We charge businesses for the service; instead of paying waste contractors to throw away surplus food, they now pay us,” Tessa explained.
She described pouncing on a Tesco representative at a conference in Coventry ten years ago, when Olio had around 10,000 users, and being dismissed. So, instead, she started with three or four corner shops in Crouch End and Finsbury Park, before working up to bigger corporate partners like Planet Organic and Pret A Manger.
The lesson for founders is that you’ve got to prove it first. “You don’t start with Tesco,” said Tessa. Build a case study at a small scale before approaching the big corporate accounts you really want. For Olio, pilots with corner shops generated the data and proof points needed to make the pitch to a national chain credible. It’s a principle that translates across virtually all sectors.
The pincer movement
Tessa was also clear that the relationship only counts once it has been prioritised internally at C-suite level. I’ve seen this over my career in newspapers and events: low-level relationship-building can feel like progress, but let’s be honest – until you get to the decision-makers, there’s no real prospect of closing a deal.
Once a large corporate does commit, the pace changes almost immediately, which Tessa described as an “incredible whiplash effect”. After years building relationships slowly and carefully, a signed client suddenly wants to be rolled out across its full estate within weeks. Tessa has learned to prepare for that shift by agreeing commercial terms before a pilot begins. That way, a successful pilot can move straight into a scaleup phase without a second negotiation, which is where deals can frustratingly slip through your fingers.
When Hamish asked her whether a personal introduction to a chief executive could have shaved a year off the Tesco deal, Tessa said ‘no’, and described the “pincer movement” used at Olio. The sales team work on building relationships low down in the organisation, while the founders go straight to the top. Speaking at industry events like SCALE, where senior decision-makers are in the audience, is part of this strategy.
“When you’re on the stage, they come to you and it changes the power dynamic. Once you’ve got a CEO excited, they send missives down the organisation and it can really help unblock conversations,” Tessa explained.
Match your pitch to the person in front of you
Any scaleup doing business with corporates knows the agony of waiting for sign-off. Tessa’s advice was to scope the proposal to match the seniority of the person in the room, rather than pitching something bigger that requires approval from someone else.
“If the contact can only authorise two stores, the pitch should be for two stores,” she said. That’s the result to aim for in the first instance.
Pilots should be paid for
Olio moved away from free pilots after finding that clients didn’t have enough incentive to make them a success. Pilots are now paid by default, though the fee is sometimes waived to keep momentum if a procurement process is particularly slow. However, if a client wants to extend a four-week pilot and run it for a further four weeks, that additional time is billed.
Tessa also pushed back on the idea of discounting pilots in exchange for marketing exposure, since early adopters and industry-leading clients typically want to promote the partnership anyway.
“In our experience, they’ve enjoyed the opportunity… they want to protect that exclusivity to get the branding benefit. I wouldn’t necessarily be going in there and dropping my price on a pilot in exchange for marketing,” said Tessa.
I couldn’t agree more. Exclusivity is a paid-for privilege. At SCALE, ‘contra’ partnerships are an important way to build our ecosystem allies and grow our audience, but exclusivity is reserved for our biggest clients, and in sectors like banking and finance, being the first name on the list is worth every penny.
Build patiently, test cheaply
Hamish Shephard, who led HelloFresh’s early US expansion, described his test-and-learn approach to finding what actually works commercially. “In our first year we did 650 tests to find viable partnership channels”. Most of them went nowhere, but he and his team showed “amazing resilience” when 95 per cent of the tests they did failed. According to Hamish, the secret to getting through it and finding success was “a really curious mindset, not a defeatist mindset.”
Curiosity may have killed the cat, but that mindset paid off when HelloFresh landed an unlikely partnership with a dog food brand.
“Everyone was like, ‘Why on earth is HelloFresh partnering with dog food?’ You don’t want to be associated with them,’” Hamish recalls. “We had to work out why it was doing well, and we started to learn that people with dogs have structured lives. They can’t not go home and choose to go out to a restaurant.” Suddenly, it became clear why dog owners would get more benefit from HelloFresh than customers in less predictable, younger urban markets. His advice to founders testing new channels was: “Move fast and keep it cheap if you can.”
Continuing the conversation
What the audience learned from Tessa and Hamish at SCALE London is that selling into enterprise can’t be unlocked through a single high-level connection. Whatever your business, and whoever you’re trying to pitch to or partner with, landing those big deals still requires old-school sales structure and discipline. And to close, you need to get in a room with the decision-makers.
For scaleups building, piloting and pitching to giants right now, SCALE Manchester on 25 November features a dedicated Selling into Enterprise session, to help UK scaleups land their first major corporate or public sector contract.
Two entrepreneurs scaling out of the North West – Steph Scholes, co-founder of corporate gifting company Needi, and Chris Gore, co-founder of IT installation specialists SPOR Group – will chat to experts from DBIST and Greater Manchester Business Growth Hub about unlocking the enterprise-level deals that have accelerated their growth. To join us, register for SCALE Manchester.

items.title: Retail industry urges home secretary to enact the protection of workers’ law
items.summary: Retail trade union Usdaw has joined forces with retail employers and their representative bodies to write to Rt Hon Shabana Mahmood, home secretary. The letter urges the government to enact the standalone offence of assaulting a shop worker during a week of national campaign activity,… This story continues at Retail industry urges home secretary to enact the protection of workers’ law Or just read more coverage at Talking Retail
items.body:
The letter urges the government to enact the standalone offence of assaulting a shop worker during a week of national campaign activity, 9-15 November.
The offence was passed by Parliament in April as part of the Crime and Policing Act. The Act also brings in Respect Orders for repeat offenders, which will be available for the police to use from 26 October.
The letter has been signed by organisations that have been campaigning for many years for action to tackle the growing levels of retail crime and violence and abuse faced by retail workers. They include: Usdaw, BRC, ACS, the Retail Trust, NBCC,
Asda, B&M, B&Q, Booths, Co-op Group, Holland & Barrett, Home Bargains, Iceland, John Lewis, Lincolnshire Co-op, Morrisons, Our Co-op, Poundland, Sainsbury’s, Southern Co-op and Tesco.
National campaign activity is being co-ordinated in retail stores and town centres by Usdaw, ACS, Retail Trust and NBCC during the week of 9-15 November, calling on the public to respect shop workers.
Joanne Thomas, Usdaw general secretary, said: “We warmly welcome the positive actions taken so far by the government in response to the retail crime epidemic they inherited. Progress has been made with the rate of shop theft reducing over the last two quarters, but much more needs to be done.
“That’s why we need the landmark legislation passed earlier this year to come into force soon as possible. The government’s investment in policing is much-needed, but officers must also have the tools to tackle retail crime and assaults on workers.
“It is brilliant to see the whole industry coming together to both welcome the steps that the Government have taken and to show their enthusiasm for the specific offence to come into effect. We are really proud to be able to help coordinate this breadth of support.”
Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium (BRC), said: “The Crime and Policing Act introduced vital new powers to allow the police to tackle the scourge of retail assault.
With over 1,600 incidents of violence and abuse against retail colleagues every day, we need to see these powers in action as soon as possible. Nobody should have to go to work fearing for their safety.”
Ed Woodall, Association of Convenience Stores (ACS) chief executive said: “The government deserves credit for recognising the impact that violence and abuse has on retailers and shop workers, and for legislating to create a standalone offence.
“We urge the government to bring the offence into force as soon as possible, giving retailers and shop workers the confidence that attacks on those serving communities will be treated with the seriousness they deserve.”
Chris Brook-Carter, chief executive of the retail industry charity, the Retail Trust, commented: “Retail workers have waited too long for stronger protection from the abuse and violence they face simply for doing their jobs.
“It is important this new protection is brought into force ahead of this year’s busy festive shopping period when unacceptable behaviour towards staff is likely to be at its worst.
“This will send a powerful message that any form of abuse will not be tolerated and remind us all to treat shop workers with more respect, kindness and courtesy in the run-up to Christmas.
Supt Lisa Maslen, head of the National Business Crime Centre (NBCC) said: “The National Business Crime Centre works closely with policing and the retail sector to tackle retail crime and improve outcomes for victims.
“Enacting the standalone offence of assaulting a shop worker will provide a clear and consistent framework for responding to these offences, helping to ensure that offenders are dealt with robustly and that victims receive the support and protection they deserve.”

items.title: Electronic shelf labels likely to cost jobs and drive up grocery prices, US report warns
items.summary: AFL-CIO calls for ban on such labels to protect consumers and workers from surveillance pricing and job cuts The universal adoption of electronic shelf labels in grocery stores across the US could cost tens of thousands of jobs and billions of dollars in lost wages while further driving up grocery costs, according to a report released on Tuesday. An analysis by the AFL-CIO Tech Institute of the label manufacturers’ own marketing materials found the universal adoption of electronic shelf labels, which are marketed to retailers as a cost-cutting measure, could cost workers between $1.6bn and $6.9bn in lost wages annually and affect between 44,223 and 191,633 jobs. Continue reading...
items.body:
The universal adoption of electronic shelf labels in grocery stores across the US could cost tens of thousands of jobs and billions of dollars in lost wages while further driving up grocery costs, according to a report released on Tuesday.
An analysis by the AFL-CIO Tech Institute of the label manufacturers’ own marketing materials found the universal adoption of electronic shelf labels, which are marketed to retailers as a cost-cutting measure, could cost workers between $1.6bn and $6.9bn in lost wages annually and affect between 44,223 and 191,633 jobs.
The policy brief – Priced Out, Pushed Out: Electronic Shelf Labels Raise Prices and Shrink Paychecks – calls for a ban on electronic labels to protect consumers and workers.
Manufacturers have hailed the labels as a way to collect huge amounts of personal data from customers, increase profits and cut labor costs.
The report argues that electronic shelf labels use the same pricing systems that allow dynamic pricing – price changes such as increasing allergy medication prices when pollen counts are high – to surveillance pricing, changing prices based on personal data.
These technologies are being implemented across the US retail industry at a time when food prices have surpassed inflation and wage gains, increasing 33% over the past seven years.
“Through our analysis, we found that the implementation of electronic shelf labels are likely going to drive prices even higher. The reason being that these labels are connected to the same algorithmic pricing software that online retailers are already using,” said Sunny Glottmann, policy and programs managers at the AFL-CIO Tech Institute and co-author of the report.
“Electronic shelf labels create the infrastructure that would make rapid algorithmic price changes easier to implement at scale, and this raises concerns for consumers that are already struggling with grocery costs.”
The report comes as several states have begun introducing legislation to ban surveillance pricing and electronic shelf labels. In April, Maryland became the first state in the US to ban surveillance pricing. Connecticut signed a ban into law in June and New Jersey signed a ban into law in July.
Electronic shelf labels “enable instantaneous price changes”, said Lauren McFerran, executive director of the AFL-CIO Tech Institute and former chairman of the National Labor Relations Board.
“This is a technology that both is enabling this kind of ‘how do we extract the absolute most money out of grocery shoppers that is humanly possible’ and ‘how do we squeeze our workers as much as is humanly possible’,” said McFerran.
A May poll released by the United Food and Commercial Workers union found 68% of Americans believe surveillance pricing will increase grocery costs and 65% say digital price tags will do the same. About 67% support banning digital price tags and surveillance pricing, with only 26% opposing a ban.
Ademola Oyefeso, vice-president of UFCW International, said that as retailers are implementing electronic shelf labels, the labor cuts occur gradually, with workers who typically change prices on shelves losing work hours.
“Slowly, if someone has a full-time job or a part-time job, they go from full-time to part-time, from part-time to no time, and that’s what’s going to start happening across the entire industry,” said Oyefeso. “We have gone with paper labels for over 100 years. It’s worked. It’s the trust stores have built with people. I know [that] you and I are paying the same price.
“If we come there on Monday, you and I are going to pay the same price on Monday, on Tuesday, on Wednesday.”
Oyefeso said workers were also consumers, and that electronic shelf labels allow price changes to occur multiple times a day.
In December, Instacart ended a pilot program practice that allowed retailers to charge online shoppers different prices for the same products after an investigation by Consumer Reports and Groundwork Collaborative found grocery prices could differ by as much as 23% between customers.
“ESLs are the embodiment of surge pricing and surveillance pricing,” Oyefeso said. “Shelf labels allow grocery shopping to become airline ticket shopping.”

items.body:
With the big day just over 100 days away, Britain’s toy shop, The Entertainer, has revealed its top 10 toy predictions for this Christmas.
Handpicked by the UK’s largest toy retailer’s expert team, the top 10 brings together a mix of much-loved household names, exciting new launches, and exclusive lines, showcasing the breadth of toys, games, and collectables to play with at The Entertainer.
The list encompasses a range of toys within a number of trending categories including nostalgic comebacks, interactive toys, viral sensations, and toys that stand the test of time.
From LEGO and iconic construction Meccano sets designed for older builders, to character favourites from Peppa Pig to Pikachu, plus viral sensations such as Clickeez – the list spans all age-groups, interests and budgets.
Old favourites with new appeal
Nostalgia is making its way onto Christmas lists for all ages, with classic brands and collectibles giving grown-ups plenty of reasons to get involved in play too.
Meccano Pro Limited Edition Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Construction Set
New for 2026, this 1:8 scale Aston Martin Formula One construction set combines the classic appeal of Meccano with the huge popularity of F1. Featuring 1,203 real metal parts, two real tools, and up to 15 hours of building time, it’s a Christmas project designed to appeal to older builders and F1 fans alike.
For ages: 18+
From price: £200, exclusive at The Entertainer
ZURU Mini Brands Really Works Vinyl Playset
Nostalgia gets a miniature makeover with this tiny working record player, which plays music from well-known artists at the drop of a needle. Combining the retro appeal of physical music with the collectability of Mini Brands, fans can build their own collection with the separately sold Mini Vinyl Capsule range.
For ages: 3+
From price: £20
As Pokémon celebrates its 30th anniversary in 2026, childhood favourite Pikachu is set to feature on Christmas lists once again. With touch sensors, a light-up tail, and sounds and movements including a headbutt and playful laugh, Battle Action Pikachu brings one of the world’s most recognisable characters to life for a new generation of fans.
For ages: 4+
From price: £50
Collect, build, and play
Collecting is no longer just about keeping toys in a box – with the latest products designed to be built, displayed, and enjoyed long after Christmas morning.
LEGO Botanicals Rocking Plants Construction Set
LEGO continues to blur the lines between play and home décor, with this charming Botanicals set allowing builders to create two pastel-coloured plant models – a delosperma named Lumi and an echeveria named Ellie. Once built, the plants can be displayed as colourful décor, making this a Christmas gift that’s designed to be enjoyed long after the building is finished.
For ages: 9+
From price: £18
When toys come to life
From learning to ride a bike to caring for a new pet, interactive toys are giving children new ways to play, with characters that respond to touch, movement, and care.
Peppa Pig Ready, Pedal, Go Peppa Bike
A new toy for this year, little ones can help Peppa learn to ride her bike by attaching her push stick and guiding her along. With over 75 sounds and phrases, Peppa responds as children play; bringing a familiar character and a real-life milestone together in one charming interactive (and encouraging) toy.
For ages: 3+
From price: £30
furReal Gabby The Grow And Roar Tiger Intearctive Pet
Already a frequent sell-out since launching this year, furReal’s Gabby responds to love and care with more than 100 combinations of sounds and movements. Children can feed, pet, and play with this cute tiger cub as she grows – making her feel more like a real furry friend than a traditional toy.
For ages: 4+
From price: £90
Primal Hatch Megalodon Electronic Pet
For children who prefer prehistoric creatures to cuddly pets, Primal Hatch offers a seriously exciting hatching experience. The water fizzes and turns red as the Megalodon begins to emerge before lights, sounds, and sensory effects bring the prehistoric creature to life.
For ages: 5+
From price: £55
From TikTok to toy box
From satisfying sounds to viral sensations, social media is helping turn unexpected products into Christmas must-haves, with trends moving from screens to school playgrounds at speed.
Clickeez Bubble Pops Keyboard Mega Mystery Figure Pack
For kids in their ASMR era, satisfying sounds are at the heart of this collectible sensory toy, with each Clickeez designed to click and clack like a real keyboard. Having racked up more than 60 million views across TikTok and Instagram last year, and with the keyboards already selling out ahead of Christmas, Clickeez shows just how quickly a viral sensation can make the leap from social media to the school playground.
For ages: 6+
From price: £30
Classic play never goes out of style
While trends come and go, classic toys continue to earn their place on Christmas lists, with traditional imaginative play proving that some favourites never go out of style.
Early Learning Centre Wooden Kitchen
A modern take on a timeless favourite, this new wooden kitchen features clicking cooking dials, raised hobs, a sink with turning taps, and a microwave with an opening door. Available exclusively at The Entertainer and selected Tesco stores, it’s one of the latest additions to the retailer’s own Early Learning Centre range, putting imaginative role play at the heart of playtime.
For ages: 3+
Price: from £60, exclusive at The Entertainer
Bluey fans can bring the world of Muffin to life with this two-level playset, complete with a living room, bedroom, kitchen, and balcony for hours of imaginative storytelling. With Muffin ranking as the third most-loved Bluey character among pre-schoolers, behind Bluey and Bingo, according to the BBC, this new set is expected to be high on fans’ Christmas lists.
For ages: 3+
Price: from £40, exclusive at The Entertainer
Geoff Sheffield, buying director, The Entertainer, said: “At The Entertainer we live for Christmas, and after months of testing and careful selection, we’re excited to reveal our top 10 toy predictions. Our list brings together some of the biggest names in toys, brand-new launches, and exclusive products that we expect to be high on Christmas lists this year”
“What really stands out about this year’s selection is the variety. From the biggest and best-loved brands to new and exclusive lines, our top 10 showcases the breadth of toys available at The Entertainer.
“We’re seeing huge interest in toys that appeal across generations, from Meccano and LEGO builds that offer hands-on, immersive experiences, to nostalgic favourites and collectables that tap into the growing ‘kidult’ market.
“Whether Christmas lists seek out popular kids’ characters, the latest viral sensation, something to build and display, or a classic toy for imaginative play, The Entertainer is the home for all types of play this festive season.”
Alongside its top 10 Christmas predictions, The Entertainer offers thousands of toys, games and collectables for all ages, from much-loved brands to its own exclusive ranges. Trending lines this year include KPop singing dolls, slime toys, and LEGO x Fast and Furious sets.
Discover The Entertainer’s full range of Christmas toys, games and collectables in-store and online, alongside its newly launched 2026 gift guide, at www.thetoyshop.com

items.body:
Leading outdoor retailer Cotswold Outdoor has launched its new brand campaign, ‘We speak outdoors’, nationwide to mark the start of the autumn and winter seasons.
The playful brand-building campaign brings the Cotswold Outdoor spirit to life through animals: creatures that call the outdoors home, and whose natural expertise means they ‘speak’ it best.
The idea is rooted in a genuine strength of the Cotswold Outdoor brand: its stores are staffed by outdoor people themselves, from hikers and climbers to wild swimmers and cyclists, who draw on their own first-hand experience to give customers expert advice in person.
The national launch will be brought to life through a coordinated floor refresh across all Cotswold Outdoor stores, alongside campaign creative across the retailer’s website and organic social channels, creating a consistent brand experience across physical and digital touchpoints.
The in-store launch will also spotlight Cotswold Outdoor’s curated autumn and winter range, including selected exclusive lines from leading outdoor brands such as Rab, Merrell, Scarpa and Mountain Equipment. Specialist product 
Underpinning the ‘We speak outdoors’ campaign is a rigorous, data-led measurement framework designed to assess the impact of brand activity and help inform Cotswold Outdoor’s future brand investment.
The campaign has been developed and delivered in partnership with Vector Media and independent creative studio Ourselves.
Jamie Kristow, CEO of Cotswold Outdoor Group, said: “‘We’re excited to launch ‘We speak outdoors’ nationwide this season. The campaign brings the brand to life through animals that know the outdoors better than anyone. It’s a playful idea, but one that perfectly reflects what sits at the heart of our brand: people who genuinely know, love and live the outdoors too.
This campaign brings that expertise to life in a distinctive way, while creating a stronger and more consistent experience for customers across our stores and digital channels. Underpinned by a rigorous and data-led approach to measuring brand effectiveness, it will also help us to better understand the impact of brand investment and inform the next stage of our growth.”
Andrew Scott, Head of Buying at Cotswold Outdoor Group, added: “Our customers come to Cotswold Outdoor because they want the right kit, trusted advice and confidence for whatever the outdoors has in store. That means combining expert advice with a carefully selected range from the best outdoor brands, including exclusive products they won’t find everywhere else.
Working closely with brands such as Rab allows us to bring customers standout products alongside the technical expertise in our stores, which is exactly what ‘We speak outdoors’ is about.”

items.body:
St Pierre, the UK’s fastest-growing continental bakery brand, is expanding its portfolio with the launch of St Pierre Chocolate & Hazelnut Filled Croissants, securing listings across Tesco, Asda, Sainsbury’s and Co-op.
The new six-pack SKU will reach more than 2,200 stores nationwide this autumn, providing retailers with a premium bakery proposition designed to tap into breakfast and snacking occasions.
Available now on promotional shippers in 387 Sainsbury’s stores and across 520 Tesco sites in the bakery aisle, the brand’s latest croissant innovation will also be available in 350 Asda stores from 14 September and 970 Co-op stores from 23 November, giving the launch significant national distribution.
Developed to help retailers capitalise on growing demand for convenient, premium bakery products, the new offering combines light, flaky layers of laminated croissant pastry with a smooth, rich chocolate and hazelnut filling, in an individually wrapped format designed for freshness and convenience.
Each pack contains six 45g croissants and has an RRP of £2.50.
Consumer testing points to strong demand for the launch, with the product achieving 86 per cent appeal and an overall preference score of 78 per cent. The research also highlighted the breadth of occasions available to retailers, with 60 per cent of consumers saying they would eat the product for breakfast, while more than half would eat it as a snack on the go.
Gill Riley, global VP marketing at St Pierre Groupe, comments: “Breakfast and snacking continue to offer significant opportunities for bakery retailers and this launch has been developed with those occasions firmly in mind. By combining a familiar and much-loved flavour pairing with the premium quality consumers expect from St Pierre, we’re giving retailers a proposition that can drive consumption across multiple occasions throughout the day.
“The consumer response has been incredibly encouraging, particularly the strength of appeal and the range of occasions for which consumers would use the product. From breakfast at home to snacks on the go, it offers retailers a versatile bakery proposition with broad consumer appeal.
“Securing listings across Tesco, Asda, Sainsbury’s and Co-op is also an important milestone for the brand, further strengthening St Pierre’s presence within continental bakery and supporting our ambition to bring more premium bakery occasions to UK shoppers.”
The launch forms part of a broader programme of innovation and distribution growth for St Pierre, following the introduction of its category-first Croissant Loaf and All Butter Croissant Rolls earlier this year. Together, the launches are extending the brand’s reach across breakfast, brunch, lunch and snacking occasions, while bringing new formats and additional choice to the bakery fixture.
St Pierre is also increasing distribution across its sweet treats portfolio this autumn. From 14 September, St Pierre Brioche Swirls and Chocolate Chip Brioche Swirls will be available in more than 350 Asda stores.
From 23 November, St Pierre Brioche Swirls will also roll into 340 Co-op stores nationwide. The six-pack Brioche Swirls combine soft, golden brioche with a creamy vanilla custard filling, while the Chocolate Chip Brioche Swirls pair vanilla custard with chocolate chips. Both products are individually wrapped for convenience, freshness and snacking on the go.

items.body:
Co-op Wholesale has announced a major investment in its vape proposition that will deliver lower upfront prices, a simpler commercial model for retail partners and a significantly expanded range.
With the forthcoming introduction of Vaping Products Duty set to bring additional complexity to the category, Co-op Wholesale is simplifying how value is delivered to retailers.
From October 2026, the wholesaler will be reducing invoice prices by up to 15 per cent across its vape range as well as simplifying its vape rebate model. Designed to help retailers navigate a changing vape market, the new proposition will deliver value directly through lower purchase prices, giving retailers greater transparency and making margins easier to manage. In addition, it will be adding over 200 new vape lines, taking its range to approximately 500 SKUs.
Value and range are two of the biggest challenges facing convenience retail partners in their stores. Through listening to its customers, Co-op Wholesale is providing solutions for both via these propositional changes.
Katie Secretan, managing director at Co-op Wholesale, said: “Retailers are navigating significant change within the vape category. This is an opportunity for us to simplify the way we manage the commercial value of vape; from rebate to price, offering our retailers a real opportunity to grow their business. We are refreshing our range, to one of the biggest in the wholesale market of over 500 SKUs and investing to deliver some of the best pricing in the market too. We’re going big, to support our retailers at a time that really matters.” 
Retail partners have today (9 September) received full details of the new proposition and range, with dedicated support, account management guidance and an invite to a retailer webinar hosted by industry experts to learn more about how to navigate the upcoming vape duty.

items.body:
Crisp-mas has come early for snack lovers as Co-op brings back its beloved Roast Potato Crisps after a three-year hiatus.
Back by popular demand, the fan favourite has returned to Co-op stores nationwide this September as part of the retailer’s eagerly anticipated festive crisp range, giving shoppers one of the first tastes of Christmas.
First launched in 2019, the crisps quickly developed a loyal fan base thanks to their surprisingly bold taste despite a seemingly simple name. More than just potato, they combine sea salt, garlic, rosemary and black pepper to recreate the seasonings that transform the humble roast potato into the star of Christmas dinner.
Ever since disappearing from shelves in 2023, shoppers have been calling for their return, with comments including:
“Bring back the Ultimate Roast Potato flavour”
“Any chance of Roast Potatoe flavour returning please?”
“Where did your roast potato crisps go?… please can we have them back?”
Now, the retailer has brought it back with a new crinkle-cut twist, joining another festive favourite, Pigs in Blankets Crisps, alongside a gourmet new edition, Wagyu Beef & Caramelised Onion flavour. Each flavour is made with carefully selected British potatoes and are hand cooked in small batches for the perfect crunch every time.
Natalie Dawe, Crisps, Snacks and Nuts Development Manager at Co-op, said: “Our crisps have developed something of a cult following over the years, with our customers regularly championing their favourites. This year, we’re delighted to bring back our Roast Potato Crisps and what I love about them is that the flavour always sparks discussion… it’s much more than meets the eye! Combining salt, garlic, rosemary and black pepper to recreate the taste of perfectly seasoned roasties.
Alongside Pigs in Blankets and our new Wagyu Beef & Caramelised Onion flavour, we’re excited to bring that early festive feeling to shoppers!”
Co-op’s Christmas crisps range:
Irresistible Ultimate Roast Potato Crinkle Cut Crisps, 150g, £1.75
Inspired by the staple of every Christmas dinner – using the herbs, seasoning and oils often used to create the perfect roast potato dish: Cornish sea salt, garlic, rosemary, black pepper and extra virgin olive oil.
Irresistible Wagyu Beef & Caramelised Onion Flavour Crisps, 150g, £1.75
New for 2026 and tapping into the growing popularity of Wagyu, this rich, gourmet-inspired recipe combines British Wagyu beef with sweet, caramelised onion.
Irresistible Pigs in Blankets Crinkle Cut Crisps, 150g, £1.75
A festive staple at Co-op returns. Each crisp is covered in a smoky, savoury, pigs in blankets seasoning, capturing the taste of everyone’s favourite Christmas side dish.

items.body:
Freemans.com announced today (9 September 2026) that its Market Place offer is already delivering strong momentum, with growth of 100% and performance that is outpacing the wider market.
The success comes after the ‘official’ launch of the retailer’s Market Place offer earlier this year, following a softer launch in Autumn 2025.
The third-party offer has been specifically designed to complement Freemans’ own-bought ranges, widening choice for customers across clothing, footwear, beauty, gifts, gadgets, power tools, home and garden.
So successful has the initiative been that Freemans has now announced an ambition to add an additional 120 brands to the Market Place’s 150 brands next year, building on a fast-expanding roster of new and established names and swelling partners tonearly 300.
Big-name brands that are set to join the digital department store in AW26 include Moda in Pelle, Draper Tools, Startrite Footwear, The Baird Group’s Ted Baker, Antique Rogue and Limehouse as well as Time Products.
At the same time, Freemans.com also announced that it was hosting a breakfast briefing, partnering with Pentagon, the marketplace solutions provider, on 17 September 2026.
Hosted by Freemans Chief Merchandising Officer, Susie Calvert and Steve Harrison, head of marketplace, both will talk through the digital department store’s market-beating growth strategy and the opportunity for famous-name third-party retail brands to partner with the retailer.
Attendees will also hear from We Are Pentagon and Warehow on how brands can overcome the practical challenges of launching on a new marketplace — from onboarding and store management through to fulfilment and returns.
Interest has been so great that the event is close to selling out with some of the top-name UK retail brands attending.
Ann Steer, CEO, Freemans.com, said, “We are moving at pace to deliver the very best digital department store offer in the UK. A blend of exclusive own-bought ranges, complemented by an edited third-party marketplace offer, underpins this ambition, coupled with a single-minded focus on shoppers over 40. It is paying dividends as we grow ahead of the market.”
“The breakfast is a chance to hear from Susie and Steve about where we have been and where we are going. We’ve already been astounded by the response and look forward to sharing and celebrating the opportunity that Freemans.com delivers both today and beyond.”
Earlier this year Freemans announced that among the latest brands to sign up, designer shoe labels including Kurt Geiger and Carvela, plus high-street favourite Dune Footwear, had come on board.
Incorporating the new brands will add more than 22,000 third-party products to the overall Freemans.com site.
Not a retailer to rest on its laurels, Freemans.com is on the lookout for even more new partners, especially in key strategic categories such as menswear, home, electricals and beauty/wellbeing.
To secure one of the last places at the breakfast, please register here.

Hotel Chocolat has announced an exclusive partnership with Deliveroo, launching initially with five of its locations - Manchester Cross Street, Chiswick, Staines, St James's and Wimbledon. Customers will be able to shop the Velvetiser, Hotel Chocolat's new boxed selections, its signature selectors, and Velvetised Creams.

“Partnering with Deliveroo gives customers a completely new way to access and send Hotel Chocolat gifts: combining the quality and originality they expect from us with greater choice and flexibility. It’s an exciting next step in how we’re growing the brand and meeting customers where they want to shop.”
Suzy McClintock, VP Consumer at Deliveroo, says: “We are building a new destination for gifting at Deliveroo. Customers are no longer using our platform just to shop for themselves but to send something special to a loved one, whether for Valentine’s Day, Christmas, a birthday and more. As a true gifting specialist, Hotel Chocolat brings real brand authority and category expertise to our retail offer, and we are excited to help them reach more consumers who are on a mission to find a meaningful last minute gift.”
2026 RTIH Innovation Awards
On demand delivery will be a key focus area at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards.
The awards are now open for entries and celebrate global retail technology innovation in a fast moving omnichannel world.
Our winners will be revealed at the 2026 RTIH Innovation Awards Ceremony, taking place at The HAC in Central London on Wednesday, 4th November.
Check out our 2025 winners here.
Our 2025 hall of fame entrants were revealed during a sold out event which took place at The HAC on 16th October and consisted of a drinks reception, three course meal, and awards ceremony presided over by award winning comedian, actress and writer Tiff Stevenson.
In his welcome speech, Scott Thompson, Founder and Editor, RTIH, said: “This is the awards’ fifth year as a physical event. We started off with just 30 people at the South Place Hotel not far from here, then moved to London Bridge Hotel, then The Barbican, and last year RIBA’s HQ in the West End.”
“But I’m conscious of the fact that, to quote the legend that is Taylor Swift, You’re only as hot as your last hit, baby. So, this year we’ve moved to our biggest venue yet, and also pulled in our largest number of entries to date and broken attendance records.”
He added: “This year’s submissions have without doubt been our best yet. To quote one of the judges: The examples of innovative developments across both traditional and digital retail spaces were truly remarkable.”
Congratulations to our winners, and a big thank you to our sponsors, judging panel, the legend that is Tiff Stevenson, and all those who attended our 2025 gathering.
Editor and Founder of Retail Technology Innovation Hub

items.body:
ZetaDisplay has extended its long-standing partnership with Spar to deliver the retailer’s first retail media network, marking a significant step in Spar’s digital transformation journey and creating new opportunities for brand partners.
This follows Zetadisplay’s recent acquisition of retailmediatools, a retail media infrastructure-as-a-service platform. The acquisition creates the first fully integrated retailer-owned media ecosystem, bridging physical in-store influence with digital advertising and precision giving retailers complete control of their retail media operations.
The rollout for Spar has begun with a pilot programme and will continue through to the end of the year. The initiative introduces a scalable retail media infrastructure designed to enhance in-store engagement, optimise the customer journey and unlock new value for both Spar and its brand partners.
ZetaDisplay’s Austria team, which has collaborated with Spar for more than a decade, will lead the project. Over the years, the partnership has delivered a series of innovative in-store digital solutions, including the evolution of dining experiences through dynamic digital menu boards, deli counter screens, kiosk ordering systems, mosaic walls as well as employee information screens.
The rollout will see the installation of hundreds of new displays, establishing a robust digital signage network that supports both retail media and broader in-store communications. The project also includes the strategic repositioning of current displays to better align with evolving shopper behaviours, leveraging ZetaDisplay’s ongoing research into customer journeys and in-store engagement.
The entire network will be powered by ZetaDisplay’s proprietary Engage Suite, which will also be implemented across Spar Slovenia’s stores. Engage Suite enables seamless content creation, scheduling and management, while providing advanced analytics and measurement tools to deliver the right message to the right audience at the right time.
Spar will retain full control over its retail media ecosystem, including the ability to approve which brands can advertise across its network, while also leveraging the platform to promote its own campaigns.
The introduction of retail media capabilities represents a significant step forward in Spar’s omnichannel strategy, strengthening how it connects digital media with the in-store experience. The new infrastructure will enable Spar greater control and flexibility across its media network, enabling more precise targeting based on time of day, location and customer behaviour. It also allows the ability to deliver more consistent, relevant messaging throughout the store, creating a seamless customer journey while opening up new opportunities for its brand partners.
Bernhard Schuch, key account manager at ZetaDisplay, comments: “The acquisition of retailmediatools marks an exciting milestone for ZetaDisplay as we expand our retail media offering. By bringing together our expertise in digital signage with retailmediatools’ retail media platform, we’re helping retailers unlock the full potential of their physical stores.
Retail media is transforming stores from places where transactions happen into powerful media channels. By combining first-party data, audience insights and strategically placed digital touchpoints, retailers such as Spar can deliver more relevant customer experiences while creating scalable new revenue opportunities.”

This launch marks the expansion of Finsbury Food Group’s licensed celebration cake portfolio and has been created in collaboration with Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products (WBDGCP). With 2026 marking the 25th anniversary since Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone first aired on the silver screen, and plenty of excitement on the horizon for Harry Potter fans, we’re thrilled to be launching this new cake to celebrate the legacy of Harry Potter and a new era ahead.
Designed to appeal to long-standing fans of the series, as well as a new generation discovering the magic of Hogwarts for the very first time, the celebration cake brings to life some of the most recognisable details from the iconic films.
Chocolate sponge and chocolate frosting is encased within rich burgundy icing with gold accents in homage to fan favourite House, Gryffindor. The Golden Snitch and Sorting Hat both feature as chocolate decorations alongside the Hogwarts crest in gold lustre detailing. The 1kg cake serves up to 16 people and is ready to make birthdays and celebrations feel worthy of a feast in the Great Hall itself.
As licensed celebration cakes continue to perform strongly across UK retail, character-led products remain a popular choice for birthdays and family occasions. With Harry Potter appealing to both younger audiences and nostalgic fans alike, Finsbury has identified a real opportunity to bring the globally loved brand to supermarket shoppers in a celebration-ready format.
Andrew Scott, brand manager at Finsbury Food Group, said: “With so much to celebrate this year within the world of Harry Potter, we felt this was the perfect moment to launch a new cake inspired by the franchise.”
“Harry Potter has an incredibly loyal fanbase, from those who grew up with the original stories and watching the films in cinemas, to younger audiences discovering the magic for the very first time.”
“The cake will become a permanent addition to Tesco’s celebration cake range, giving fans a spell-binding option for birthdays and special occasions throughout the year.”

items.body:
In Kind Direct, the UK’s leading product giving charity, and Tesco have partnered together since September 2022 to run their ‘Buy 2, we’ll donate 1’ campaign and this spring, ran the campaign for the sixth time.
Designed to unlock product donations from some of the leading hygiene brands, the partnership has supported families across the country gain access to over 6 
This year, the campaign included products from seventeen leading hygiene brands, Pampers, Andrex, Kleenex, Tena, Bodyform, Simple, Aquafresh, Sensodyne, Domestos, Sure, Dove, Surf, Wilkinson-Sword, Persil, Corsodyl, Vaseline, and Comfort. Resulting in over 1.33 million personal care and household hygiene items being donated across 
Across the 4-year partnership, Tesco and In Kind Direct have:
- generated 6.3 million essential personal care and household hygiene items
- reached 5,320 charitable organisations across the UK, helping to support the families currently experiencing hygiene poverty across the UK.
- This includes 8,015,916 period pads; 1,229,939 deodorants; 742,726 toilet rolls; and 235,680 toothbrushes over the last five years.
- Hygiene products are helping restore confidence in many ways, from providing children with a toothbrush alongside oral care information, to ensuring parents can support their children’s needs without added stress.
Together, In Kind Direct and Tesco have facilitated wide-scale product donations from well-known brands making it one of the largest cross-sector product donation schemes of its kind.
With the number of brands taking part increasing annually, this partnership reinforces the need for cross-sector collaboration across the FMCG category to support families in need
By forging an alliance of 
Michael Gidney, CEO of In Kind Direct comments: “We’re really proud of what we’ve been able to achieve over the last 4 years, as a result of our partnership with Tesco and many of the UK’s leading hygiene brands. Distributing more than 6m essential products to date is a huge achievement, but across the UK we hear from people in our network about what it means every day. It’s the dignity offered to the woman who had been using socks in place of period products; the excitement on the six-year-old boy’s face who had his own toothbrush for the first time; the way homeless service users describe how it feels to access personal care products. And the impact won’t stop there. We are seeing more and more brands willing to come together to help end hygiene poverty – a cause that is much bigger than all of us.
No single charity or brand can solve this alone. It required true cross-collaboration from charities, retailers and brands who are committed to making a difference in people’s lives.”
Tommy Maier, category buying manager – beauty & personal care at Tesco, said: “We’re proud of the impact that this campaign has had helping millions of families across the UK access hygiene products. We would like to thank all our customers, colleagues and the brands that supported this worthwhile cause and helped make a real difference to those in need.”
A volunteer at Darnall Community Nursery, based in Sheffield, whose charity accesses products through In Kind Direct’s network, commented: “
A volunteer at Beyond Limits, based in County Durham, commented: “Shaving products are included in care packs for gentlemen on low incomes. Many of the recipients have told us how long it had been since they had proper shaving products, and how it helped them feel clean, confident, and more themselves again – particularly when preparing for special occasions.”
Branchton Community Centre, based in Scotland, commented: “Providing a struggling family with essentials like free toilet roll and laundry detergent may seem small, but it can have a powerful impact. These basic items relieve immediate financial pressure, restore a sense of dignity, and help families maintain hygiene and comfort during difficult times. By removing the stress of choosing between necessities, this simple act of support can free up limited resources for food, utilities, or school needs and to remind people that they’re not alone, strengthening both wellbeing and community connections.”
A staff member at Teth Youth & Adult Services, based in London, commented: “By having access to items such as diapers, wipes, and other baby necessities, we were able to relieve some of that pressure. One mother shared that the essentials she received meant she could redirect the little money she had toward healthy food for her family, while still feeling confident her baby’s needs were met.”

items.body:
Growth Studio is delighted to announce Holland & Barrett has partnered with Breakout Wellness UK, becoming the accelerator programme’s founding retail partner.
As the UK’s largest health and wellness retailer, Holland & Barrett will bring its health, wellness and retail expertise to help the programme identify, unlock and champion the success of ten high potential founders.
Holland & Barrett join a powerful consortium of global partners and UK specialists, ready to discover and lend their support to exciting, emerging new wellness brands. Breakout Wellness UK business experts include HSBC Innovation Banking, TikTok Shop, Bird & Bird LLP, Somerce, Finishing Line, Taylored Consultancy and some of the UK’s biggest consumer focused VC’s.
Breakout Wellness UK was launched in Spring 2026, designed to help the UK’s most promising, high growth wellness founders scale faster, become retail-ready and build globally successful brands.
The programme will include businesses spanning gut health, functional nutrition, hydration, energy and recovery, longevity, sleep, stress management and women’s health.
Applicants from all over the UK are currently being reviewed, ready to showcase their products at the Breakout Wellness UK breakfast launch on 22 September and subsequently commence their intensive eight-week programme.
Whilst London accounted for roughly half of applicants (54%), nearly half were from outside the capital — a sign of the depth of wellness entrepreneurship across the UK.
Guy Farmer, chief commercial officer at Holland & Barrett, said: “Health and wellness is moving fast, and Holland & Barrett has always been at the forefront of innovation..
Partnering with Breakout Wellness is a natural next step, bringing together the creativity and innovation of emerging founders with our scale, health and retail expertise, and trusted colleague advice model to help promising brands develop and grow.
Ultimately, it’s about bringing great new health and wellness solutions to more customers and delivering on our mission to help people live better for longer.”
Paul Finch, co-founder of Growth Studio and chief architect of Breakout Wellness UK, says: “We are delighted to welcome Holland & Barrett as our first retail partner to Breakout Wellness UK. As the UK’s leading, largest and most respected wellness retailer, we couldn’t have chosen a better founding partner.
Many wellness founders innovate incredible products that scale rapidly through social commerce. However they often lack the retail knowledge they need, such as how and what to present to buyers, understanding retail operations and systems, and crucially, how to maintain listing growth and longevity.
Having the Holland & Barrett team help select and coach our cohort, whilst providing guidance to our startup ecosystem is absolutely invaluable. We cannot wait to start working together”
As a first of its kind, Breakout Wellness UK has secured the backing of leading wellness business leaders and entrepreneur Ambassadors including Hamish Grierson, co-founder and CEO at Thriva, Alana McFarlane Kempner, Founder and CEO at The Gut Stuff, Frances Lucraft, founder of Grace and Green, Henry Goldsmith, co-founder of SULT, Frida Redknapp, founder of Frood and Arjun Sofat, co-founder and CEO of FreeSoul, one of UK’s fastest growing business with £42m revenue.
Growth Studio brings more than a decade of experience designing and delivering accelerator programmes internationally. Following the success of its inaugural Breakout Beauty UK programme, which attracted almost 300 applications in 2026, the team expects demand for Breakout Wellness UK to be even stronger.
The programme will culminate in a Grand Finale in November, where each founder will showcase their business and pitch to an audience of leading retailers and investors. Two winners will each receive a TikTok Shop support package worth £150,000 to help accelerate their growth.

items.body:
Hotel Chocolat has partnered with Deliveroo to bring chocolate gifting on demand, giving customers a new way to send considered chocolate gifts when the moment calls for it.
Launching initially with five Hotel Chocolat locations – Manchester Cross Street, Chiswick, Staines, St James’s and Wimbledon – customers will be able to order a curated selection of Hotel Chocolat products directly through Deliveroo.
For more than two decades, Hotel Chocolat has continued to challenge what a chocolate gift can be. Combining its deep knowledge of cacao with original recipes, distinctive flavours and considered presentation, the chocolatier has built its gifting range around helping customers find something that feels personal to the recipient.
The new exclusive partnership marks the latest evolution of that approach. By bringing Hotel Chocolat to Deliveroo, customers can turn the thought of someone into a meaningful gesture when the moment arises: whether celebrating good news, saying thank you, marking a birthday, bringing something special to a host or simply showing someone they’re being thought of.
The range brings together some of Hotel Chocolat’s most distinctive gifting propositions. Customers will be able to shop the Velvetiser®, Hotel Chocolat’s new boxed selections, its signature selectors, and Velvetised Creams.
The partnership responds to clear consumer demand, with searches on the Deliveroo app for ‘Hotel Chocolat’ up by more than 40% in the year to June 2026, compared to the 12 months prior.
The launch comes as Hotel Chocolat prepares for the biggest gifting period of the year, with Christmas gifting, including Advent calendars and stocking fillers, set to join the Deliveroo range later this year.
Carrie Martin, UK general manager at Hotel Chocolat, said: “Thoughtful gifting has always been at the heart of Hotel Chocolat, and we’re constantly looking at how we can make it easier for customers to mark the moments that matter.
Partnering with Deliveroo gives customers a completely new way to access and send Hotel Chocolat gifts: combining the quality and originality they expect from us with greater choice and flexibility. It’s an exciting next step in how we’re growing the brand and meeting customers where they want to shop.”
Suzy McClintock, VP consumer at Deliveroo, said: “We are building a new destination for gifting at Deliveroo. Customers are no longer using our platform just to shop for themselves but to send something special to a loved one, whether for Valentine’s Day, Christmas, a birthday and more. As a true gifting specialist, Hotel Chocolat brings real brand authority and category expertise to our retail offer, and we are excited to help them reach more consumers who are on a mission to find a meaningful last-minute gift.”

items.title: Zara owner Inditex defies high street gloom as sales rise on demand for warmer clothes
items.summary: Zara owner Inditex continued to win over customers unconvinced by cheaper online shops like Shein, which launched its lacklustre initial public offering in Hong Kong this month.
items.body:
Zara owner Inditex defies high street gloom as sales rise on demand for warmer clothes
- See more This is Money on Google - save us as a Preferred Source
Zara owner Inditex continues to defy the high street gloom after reporting a rise in sales in recent weeks as shoppers seek out warmer clothes.
The group, which also owns Bershka, said its autumn and winter clothing lines had been 'well received'.
Sales rose by 9 per cent between August 1 and September 7 compared to a year ago, despite the heatwaves and war in the Middle East, which have triggered a slump in consumer confidence and spending.
While depreciation charges ate into profits, the group's strong recent sales indicated it continues to outpace rivals such as H&M.
It also continues to win over customers unconvinced by cheaper online shops like Shein, which launched its lacklustre initial public offering in Hong Kong this month.
Inditex generated sales of €11billion in its second quarter from May to July, representing a strong performance in a summer of high energy prices and weak consumer sentiment amid the ongoing war in Iran.
Higher sales: Zara owner Inditex saw sales rise by 9% from August 1 to September 7 compared to the same month a year ago
But its second-quarter gross profit margin was 56.7 per cent, slightly below analysts' expectations as the conflict increased costs.
The retailer group's profits rose sharply to €3.85billion in its first half as chief executive Óscar García Maceiras hailed the 'extraordinary capabilities of our teams'.
A final dividend of €0.875 per share will be paid on November 2, 2026.
Under chair Marta Ortega, Inditex has sought to elevate its main Zara brand with upscale flagship shops and collaborations with high-profile designers and photographers.
Earlier this year Zara hired John Galliano, the former creative director of Dior, as a 'guest designer', with a first collection set to launch this month.
As well as Zara, Inditex owns the Massimo Dutti, Pull & Bear and Bershka brands. It also owns Lefties, which it is currently expanding.
First launched in 1993 as an outlet to sell leftover Zara stock, Lefties has since evolved into a standalone value fashion chain and one of the fastest growing and most in-demand brands under the Inditex umbrella.
According to the latest results, Lefties’ store count at 31 July 2026 was 223, up from 210 stores the same date last year. It has since added its first UK store at Liverpool One shopping centre, opened on August 27.
This launch is to be followed by a store at Lakeside shopping centre, Essex and Gateshead’s Metrocentre shopping centre this autumn.
